column10: Note
The US flagship retrofit. Design 1999–2001, install 2001–2006, three segment cutovers, ~8 months shadow running. Roughly $48M per km. No civil works; throughput up from ~20 tph.
Validated through thousands of scenarios on a full-system simulator running production software before any test train moved in Manhattan.
The most substantial current US CBTC implementation. Fleet- and function-phased.
Single-prime contract, ~$398M, 78 railcars, vehicles co-designed for the CBTC. First US mass-transit line certified for unattended operation.
An airport system rather than a metro, and one of only two long-standing US GoA 4 operations.
An early automated train control system predating modern CBTC standards; 25+ years of tenure informs current procurement practice.
Frequently overlooked in US benchmark sets.
Some sections mixed-mode.
Partial GoA 4 operation in certain sections.
Hornell, NY manufacturing is a stated competitive advantage.
Emphasis on open interfaces and Buy America compliance.
The greenfield showcase: the first modern metro to open at GoA 4. 100% platform screen doors from day one. ~650,000 daily riders. €650–750M for the full line.

The brownfield paradigm shift: converted under traffic over a five-year phased cutover, PSDs retrofitted to 86% of platforms over five years. ~1.5M daily riders. €700M+. Throughput rose from ~20 to 27 tph.
The longest uninterrupted GoA 4 record in continental Europe. 34 three-car driverless sets; unattended operation was a founding requirement, not a retrofit.
Turnkey contract ~€700M covering signaling, power, comms, SCADA, PSDs, control centre, depot and rolling stock. M4 Nordhavn opened 28 Mar 2020; a 4.5 km Sydhavn extension 22 Jun 2024.
Forty years of driverless operation — the deepest GoA 4 operating record behind any Western supplier's claims.
Throughput rose from 18 to 24 tph on unchanged civil infrastructure.
Delivered under the Metronet PPP model, whose contractual structure is as instructive as its engineering.
Multi-signaling architecture at scale: CBTC in the core, conventional signaling on the outer branches, with transitions in service.
The LTA model for fully automated network expansion; fleet-phased retrofit on existing lines.
Operated by Keolis-MHI. A reference case for public acceptance of unattended operation at scale.
